draft.title: Coastal processes
card: Coastal processes are the natural actions that shape a coast. The main ones are waves, tides, currents and wind.
Waves
Waves are the biggest shaper of most coasts. They break against cliffs and headlands and wear the rock away. This is erosion. Over time it can leave rock platforms, cliffs and caves.
Tides and currents

Tides are the daily rise and fall of the sea. They change how far up the shore waves can reach. Waves that hit a beach at an angle push sand along the shore, and this is called longshore drift. It moves sand along a beach, and a current can carry it further.
Wind
Wind blows dry sand from the beach inland. Sand can build up into dunes, especially where plants trap it.
draft.remember: Waves wear rock away and move sand along the shore. Wind moves sand inland to build dunes.

a.q: Waves keep crashing against a headland on the coast of New South Wales. What is the main effect on the rock over time?
opts: It is worn away by erosion
It is built up by wind-blown sand
It is covered by the rising tide
It is turned into a sandy beach
a.why: Breaking waves wear rock away, and this is erosion. Wind-blown sand does build dunes, but that happens on sandy shores and not on a rocky headland.
a.clue: Think about what waves do to hard rock.

b.q: Waves hit Mia's local beach at an angle, and over some years sand slowly shifts from the south end to the north end. Which process is mainly moving the sand?
opts: Longshore drift
Wind carrying sand inland
Waves eroding a headland
The daily rise and fall of the tide
b.why: Waves that hit a beach at an angle push sand along the shore, which is longshore drift. Wind moves sand inland, not along the beach, and tides change how far up the shore waves reach but do not push sand along it.
b.clue: Which process moves sand along the shore, not inland?

a.best: It is worn away by erosion

problems.detail: Longshore drift is explained under the heading 'Tides and currents', but the card says waves cause it. Students could think longshore drift is a tidal or current process. It would be clearer under Waves, or with the heading changed.

proposal.title: Coastal processes
card: Waves
